subject: History
description: INC: founding, early phase, moderates vs extremists, key sessions

questions.stem: INDIAN NATIONAL CONGRESS was founded in 1885 by:
questions.explanation: INC FOUNDED 28 December 1885, BOMBAY — Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College. FOUNDER: ALLAN OCTAVIAN HUME (retired British civil servant; Scottish; called 'father of INC'). FIRST PRESIDENT: WOMESH CHANDRA BANNERJEE. FIRST SESSION: 72 delegates from various provinces. THEORIES of why HUME founded: (a) 'safety valve' for educated discontent (some historians); (b) genuine sympathy + nationalist shaping (others). EARLY DEMANDS: more Indian representation, civil service reform, councils. DIDN'T ASK for independence till MUCH later. HUME's Indian collaborators: Surendranath Banerjee, Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta, Dinshaw Wacha, M.G. Ranade, Badruddin Tyabji.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: FIRST SESSION of INC (1885) was held in which city?
questions.explanation: 1st INC SESSION: 28-31 Dec 1885, BOMBAY (originally planned at Poona but cholera outbreak shifted to Bombay). At Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College. WC BANNERJEE presided over 72 delegates. SUBSEQUENT presidents (early years): Dadabhai Naoroji (3 times — 1886, 1893, 1906), Badruddin Tyabji (1887, first Muslim Pres), George Yule (1888, first European/Englishman), Surendranath Banerjee (1895, 1902), R.C. Dutt, Pherozeshah Mehta, Lal Mohan Ghose. NEHRU presided over LAHORE (1929) — adopted Purna Swaraj resolution. SUBHAS BOSE — Haripura 1938 + Tripuri 1939 (resigned). MAULANA AZAD — longest serving Pres (1940-46).

questions.stem: INC SPLIT into MODERATES + EXTREMISTS at the SURAT SESSION of:
questions.explanation: SURAT SPLIT (1907) — INC fractured between MODERATES (G.K. Gokhale, Pherozeshah Mehta, Surendranath Banerjee — wanted gradual reforms via constitutional means; faith in British justice) + EXTREMISTS (Bal Gangadhar TILAK, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal — 'LAL-BAL-PAL'; wanted SWARAJ via Swadeshi, boycott, mass mobilisation). Trigger: dispute over presidential candidate Rash Behari Ghosh + over reaffirming Calcutta resolutions on Swadeshi/Boycott. Tilak: 'Swaraj is my BIRTHRIGHT'. Extremists walked out. INC weakened ~10 years till LUCKNOW PACT (1916) reunited factions + INC + Muslim League. Modreates' golden phase ~1885-1905; extremists' phase ~1905-1918; mass-movement phase ~1918+ (Gandhian era).

questions.stem: PURNA SWARAJ (Complete Independence) resolution was adopted at the LAHORE SESSION of:
questions.explanation: LAHORE SESSION (Dec 1929) — JAWAHARLAL NEHRU as Pres. PURNA SWARAJ resolution adopted; tricolour hoisted at midnight on banks of RAVI river. 26 JAN 1930 declared as 1st INDEPENDENCE DAY (people pledged Purna Swaraj). Date later kept as REPUBLIC DAY (Constitution adoption 26 Jan 1950). Earlier INC stance: DOMINION STATUS (within British Empire, like Canada, Australia). Shift to FULL INDEPENDENCE was DECISIVE — set tone for Civil Disobedience (1930), Salt March, etc. NEHRU REPORT (1928) earlier had asked for Dominion; British rejected → INC moved to PURNA SWARAJ. CONTEXT — younger generation (Nehru, Bose, Gandhian extremists) influenced by Russian Revolution + global decolonisation pushed for radical demands.

questions.stem: FIRST WOMAN President of INC was:
questions.explanation: ANNIE BESANT — first woman INC president (1917, CALCUTTA SESSION). Irish-British theosophist, women's rights activist, Indian freedom advocate. Founded HOME RULE LEAGUE in India (1916; concurrent with Tilak's). Wrote 'NEW INDIA' newspaper. Faced internment by British (1917) → INC + nation rallied → made her president as protest. Came to India 1893 (with Theosophical Society, HQ at ADYAR, Madras). SAROJINI NAIDU (1925, Kanpur) = 1st INDIAN woman INC President; 'NIGHTINGALE OF INDIA'; later first woman GOVERNOR (UP, 1947-49). NELLIE SENGUPTA (1933) = third woman pres. Other prominent women: Aruna Asaf Ali (Quit India), Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (UN GA Pres 1953), Kasturba Gandhi, Kamala Nehru.

questions.stem: QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT was launched at INC's BOMBAY SESSION (1942) under:
questions.explanation: QUIT INDIA / 'Bharat Chhodo' — passed at BOMBAY (Gowalia Tank Maidan, now AUGUST KRANTI MAIDAN), 8 AUG 1942. GANDHI's 'DO OR DIE' speech — call for mass civil disobedience against British. Trigger: failure of CRIPPS MISSION (1942), urgency to leverage WW2. RESULT: top leaders ARRESTED next day (Gandhi, Nehru, Patel, Azad jailed); spontaneous mass uprising (1942-44) — strikes, sabotage, parallel govts (e.g., Satara, Tamluk, Talcher). British crushed it brutally — over 100,000 imprisoned, 1000+ killed. CRIPPS MISSION earlier (March 1942) — Sir Stafford Cripps came offering Dominion Status post-WW2 + provincial autonomy + right to secede; Gandhi famously called it 'A POST-DATED CHEQUE on a CRASHING BANK'. SUBHAS BOSE had left INC by 1939 + was leading INA in SE Asia.

questions.stem: DADABHAI NAOROJI is famous for theory of:

options.option_text: Drain of wealth (Indian wealth to Britain)

questions.explanation: DADABHAI NAOROJI (1825-1917; 'GRAND OLD MAN OF INDIA') — pioneered DRAIN THEORY: Britain extracted wealth from India via salaries paid in London, military expenses charged to India, civil service pensions, profits remitted home, etc. Estimated drain at ~£30-40 million / year. Wrote 'POVERTY AND UN-BRITISH RULE IN INDIA' (1901). 1ST INDIAN ELECTED to BRITISH PARLIAMENT (Liberal Party, Finsbury Central, London, 1892). Made first scientific estimate of India's national income (1867-68) — found per capita ~₹20/year (extreme poverty). 3-time INC President (1886, 1893, 1906). Indians proudly called him 'GRAND OLD MAN'. M.G. RANADE + R.C. DUTT also worked on Indian economy. Modern history considers Drain Theory mostly accurate, with refinements.
